newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish militant in Hebron held without trial.
newsitem.headline: Jewish militant in Hebron held without trial.

text.p: A Jewish militant leader was arrested on Sunday in the first of a series of actions Israel said was necessary to peacefully hand over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule.

Noam Federman, a former leader of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement, was removed from his home in the Hebron area at 5 a.m., his wife Elisheva told Israel Radio. She said they came with an order to hold him without trial for two months.

"Arrests are being made because for the moment all must be done so that the handover from one side to the other side in Hebron will be a quiet handover," Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said when asked about the action.
On Saturday Kahalani had said Israel would detain dozens of Jewish militants who might actively oppose a turnover of Hebron. He said such "extremists" might try to open fire.

The Kach movement was founded by U.S.-born Rabbi Meir Kahane who campaigned for the expulsion of Arabs from areas under Israeli rule. Kahane was assassinated in New York in 1990. Kach has been officially outlawed by Israel.

Israel and the PLO appear on the verge of closing a deal to hand over the city to Palestinian rule. Hebron is the last of seven West Bank cities due to be handed over under an interim peace deal signed in September 1995.

It is also the most sensitive, holy to Moslems and Jews as the traditional burial place of the biblical Abraham. It is the only West Bank town where Jews -- 400 of them -- live and study among Arabs, who number about 100,000.
Asked if the redeployment was close, Kahalani told Israel Radio on Sunday: "We all believe it's already on the threshold of being completed."

The city is a flashpoint of violence. In February 1994 Baruch Goldstein, a Jew from Kiryat Arba settlement adjacent to Hebron, shot dead 29 Arabs at prayer in the tomb, also known as al-Ibrahimi mosque. Survivors beat him to death.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the Likud Party seeks to modify the Hebron accord signed by the previous Labour-led government to safeguard settlers in the heart of the city. Palestinians reject any changes.
Palestinian officials said on Saturday they hoped to clinch a deal on Hebron during next week's Middle East economic conference in Cairo.
But Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah said critical issues had yet to be resolved.
